lessons.title: From source files to an executable
lessons.intro:
C17; standard headers such as stdio.h, stdlib.h, string.h, and limits.h are assumed where used. C separates preprocessing, compilation, and linking. A header declares an interface; an object file contains compiled definitions. Compile every implementation file and link the resulting objects once. Read diagnostics by stage: a syntax error differs from a missing definition at link time. The commands here use GCC with portable C17; compiler flags are tool-specific. Warnings help catch suspicious code but a successful compilation is not proof of valid memory access.

lessons.title: Integer representation and conversions
lessons.intro:
C17; standard headers such as stdio.h, stdlib.h, string.h, and limits.h are assumed where used. C integer types have ranges, not arbitrary precision. sizeof(char) is one C byte; CHAR_BIT tells how many bits it contains. Do not assume int is always 32 bits. Unsigned arithmetic wraps, but signed overflow is undefined behavior. Integer promotion and signed/unsigned conversions happen before arithmetic and comparisons. A cast before division changes the operation; a cast after division cannot recover its discarded fraction.
